content:
`pwdResetRequired` is declared as a nullable `Integer` flag. Any consumer doing `if (resp.getPwdResetRequired())` or comparing with `== 1` can hit an NPE / unboxing failure when the field is not populated (e.g. deserialized legacy payloads or code paths that forget to set it). Prefer a primitive/boxed boolean with a safe default, or document the null semantics.

Suggested: `private Boolean pwdResetRequired = Boolean.FALSE;`

content:
The auto-fill field names here do not match the global MetaObjectHandler, which only fills properties named `createdAt` and `updatedAt` (see MybatisPlusConfig#metaObjectHandler: strictInsertFill("createdAt") / strictInsertFill("updatedAt") / strictUpdateFill("updatedAt")). Because these properties are named `createTime`/`updateTime`, the fill handler can never set them.

Since fields annotated with `FieldFill.INSERT/INSERT_UPDATE` are included in the generated INSERT/UPDATE SQL unconditionally, they will be written as NULL, overriding the column defaults (`create_time DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`, `update_time ... ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`), so the audit timestamps end up empty. This is also inconsistent with the rest of the module (SysUser/SysGroup/SysRole/BizCustomer all use `createdAt`/`updatedAt`).

Fix by aligning with the handler (explicit column mapping keeps the existing DB columns), or alternatively extend MetaObjectHandler to also fill `createTime`/`updateTime`.

content: `LIMIT 1` without `ORDER BY` on a multi-row join result is non-deterministic in MySQL. When a user holds several roles (`sys_user_role` has multiple rows), `role_name` and `role_id` are picked from an arbitrary row, and since the `role_name` sub-query joins `sys_role` while the `role_id` sub-query queries `sys_user_role` directly, the two can even be resolved from different rows, producing an inconsistent `role_id`/`role_name` pair. Make the pick deterministic (and identical to the one used in `ORDER BY`) by adding an explicit inner ordering, e.g. `... WHERE ur.user_id = u.id ORDER BY r.id ASC LIMIT 1`.
